tagline: A tool that explains HL7® v2 messages
intro: Free, in plain words, and private: everything runs in your browser.
dropFile: Drop the file here to open it
privacyLine: Your message never leaves your browser.
dropHint: You can also drop a .hl7 or .txt file on the box.
notice: For learning and testing only. Explanations may contain mistakes. Check against the official HL7 standard and test before using anything in production. Do not paste real patient data unless your organization allows it.
placeholder: Paste an HL7 v2 message here
samplePrompt: No message at hand? Try a sample:
sampleReplace: This replaces the message in the box.

samples.v27-oru-r01: Lab result with coded values (ORU^R01, v2.7)
samples.v29-adt-a04: Register a patient, two mistakes on purpose (ADT^A04, v2.9)

factsNote: Field names, data types and repeat rules are shown as in HL7 v{version}. Older versions can differ. Many fields have a version note that says how.

textBoxNote: Text boxes change line endings to LF. This is normal.

messageViewHint: Click any part of the message to see its explanation. Keyboard: arrow keys move, Enter opens, Esc closes.
panelEmpty: Click any part of the message, or a field name, to see its explanation.
componentNamesNote: Component names follow HL7 v2.9, or the last version that has the data type.

usageTitle: How often this field is filled in real messages

typeGloss.ID: a code from an HL7 table

addedLater: This field was added in v{since}, but the message says v{version}. The sender may use a newer version than it says, or a custom field.
addedLaterChosen: This field was added in v{since}. It does not exist in v{version}, the version you picked.
codeAddedLater: Code {code} was added in v{since}, but the message says v{version}.
codeAddedLaterChosen: Code {code} was added in v{since}. It does not exist in v{version}, the version you picked.
codeRemoved: Code {code} was removed after v{until}, but the message says v{version}.
codeRemovedChosen: Code {code} was removed after v{until}. It does not exist in v{version}, the version you picked.
codeRemovedAuto: Code {code} was removed after v{until}. It does not exist in v{version}, the version the page uses.
tipHint: advice from practice, not part of the standard
namesNote: Field names, data types and rules follow HL7 v{version}.

checks.title: Message checks
checks.summaryNone: No differences from HL7 v{version} found.
checks.summaryNoVersion: Checked without a version: {counts}. The field checks wait until you pick {pick} in "Explain as version".
checks.summaryNoneNoVersion: No problems found. The field checks wait until you pick {pick} in "Explain as version".
checks.summaryNoFields: Checked against HL7 v{version}: {counts}. Field checks are available only for HL7 v{latest}.
checks.summaryNoneNoFields: No problems found. Field checks are available only for HL7 v{latest}.
checks.listCopied: List copied. It holds no values from the message.
checks.notChecked: Not checked yet: codes, segment order, parts inside fields, lengths, conditional rules and local rules (the interface spec of your partner).
checks.pickVersion: Pick {pick} in "Explain as version" to check the fields too.
checks.fieldsSkipped: Field checks are available only for HL7 v{latest}. The other checks still ran.
checks.statusSkipped: Not checked for HL7 v{version}: fields that are withdrawn, not used or kept only for backward compatibility.
checks.checkedPicked: The fields were checked against HL7 v{version}, the version you picked.
checks.toolRule: The tool's own rule, not an HL7 rule.

sentences.S1-not-first: The message does not start with MSH (or FHS or BHS in a batch file). The tool used the default delimiters.
sentences.S1-no-msh: The text has no MSH segment, so the tool cannot read it as a message.
sentences.S2-too-short: MSH-2 has fewer than 2 characters. The tool needs at least the component and repetition characters to read the message.
sentences.S2-no-truncation: MSH-2 has 4 encoding characters. {versionName} defines 5: the fifth is the truncation character (usually #). Many systems leave it out, and truncation is optional.
sentences.S2-long: MSH-2 has 5 encoding characters. {versionName} defines 4. The fifth (truncation) character comes in v2.7.
sentences.S2-too-long: MSH-2 has {length} encoding characters. No HL7 version defines more than 5.
sentences.S3a: The segment name has {length} characters. HL7 segment names have exactly 3.
sentences.S3b: The segment name has characters other than capital letters and digits. All segment names that HL7 defines use only these.
sentences.S4: Segments end with {terminator}. HL7 requires a single CR at the end of each segment. Files often use LF, and most engines accept it.
sentences.S5: Segments end in more than one way (CR, LF or CRLF). HL7 requires a single CR at the end of each segment. Files often use LF, and most engines accept it.
sentences.S6-unclosed: An escape sequence is not closed: the escape character has no closing pair.
sentences.S6-unknown: An escape sequence uses a code that {versionName} does not define.
sentences.S6-hex: A hex escape sequence (code {code}) does not have whole pairs of hex digits.
sentences.S6-later: The escape code {code} (truncation character) exists only from HL7 v{since}. {versionName} does not define it.
sentences.S6-formatting: The text formatting command {code} is defined only for FT (formatted text) fields. This field has data type {type}.
sentences.S7: The text holds {count} messages (MSH segments). HL7 allows this in a batch file. The tool explains and checks the text as one message.
sentences.V1-empty: MSH-12 (the version) is empty. HL7 requires it in every version.
sentences.V1-unknown: MSH-12 does not hold an HL7 version that the tool knows.
sentences.V2: The message says v{message}. This is a real HL7 version, but older than 2.3. The tool explains versions 2.3 to 2.9.
sentences.V3-fields: The message says v{message}, but it fills fields of a later version ({fields}). It may follow v{since}.
sentences.V3-encoding: The message says v{message}, but MSH-2 has 5 characters. The fifth (truncation) character comes in v{since}. The message may follow v{since} or later.
sentences.V3-parts: The message says v{message}, but MSH-12 has parts. MSH-12 has parts from v{since}. The message may follow v{since} or later.
sentences.F1: This field does not exist in {versionName}. It was added in v{since}.
sentences.F2: {versionName} defines {last} fields for this segment. This field comes after the last one. It may be a local field.
sentences.F2-local: {versionName} defines {last} fields for this segment. This field comes after the last one. It may be a local field: from v2.5 HL7 allows local fields at the end of a segment, but advises against them.
sentences.F3: This field is withdrawn in {versionName}, but it is filled.
sentences.F4: This field is not used (X) in {versionName}, but it is filled.
sentences.F5: In {versionName} this field is kept only for backward compatibility. HL7 may withdraw it later.
sentences.F6: Required in {versionName}, but it is empty.
sentences.F7-once: Repeats {count} times. In {versionName} this field does not repeat. If the repetition character was not meant as a repeat, check how the sender writes it.
sentences.F7: Repeats {count} times. In {versionName} this field may repeat up to {max} times.
sentences.D1-format: The value is not a date of the form {form}.
sentences.D1-calendar: The value is not a real date.
sentences.D2-format: The value is not a date and time of the form {form} (data type {type}).
sentences.D2-calendar: The value is not a real date and time (data type {type}).
sentences.D3-format: The value is not a time of the form {form}.
sentences.D3-calendar: The value is not a real time on a 24-hour clock.
sentences.D4-format: The value is not a number (data type NM). Only an optional + or -, digits and one decimal point are allowed.
sentences.D4-point: From v2.8 a digit must come before the decimal point: write 0.5, not .5.
sentences.D5-format: The value is not a whole number of 0 or more (data type SI).
sentences.D5-range: From v2.5 a sequence ID (SI) is a number from 0 to 9999.
sentences.G1: A local segment (Z-segment). HL7 allows it. The tool cannot check it. Lines with this segment: {count}.
sentences.G2: The tool does not check this segment yet. Lines with this segment: {count}.

rules.S1: Every HL7 message starts with the MSH segment. Its first characters set the delimiters for the rest of the message. A batch file may start with FHS or BHS, and then hold messages that each start with MSH.
rules.S2: MSH-2 lists the special characters: component (^), repetition (~), escape (\), sub-component (&), and in newer versions the truncation character (#). The number changes by version: v2.3 to v2.6 allow 2 to 4 (the escape and sub-component characters may be left out), v2.7 defines 4, and v2.8 and later define 5.
rules.S3a: HL7 segment names have exactly 3 characters. The name is the first 3 characters of the segment.
rules.S3b: All segment names that HL7 defines use capital letters and digits. This is the tool's own rule, not a written HL7 rule.
rules.S4: HL7 ends every segment with a carriage return (CR, hex 0D), in every version. The standard does not allow LF or CRLF. Many files and engines use LF anyway, so the tool shows this as a note.
rules.S5: HL7 ends every segment with a carriage return (CR, hex 0D), in every version. The standard does not allow LF or CRLF. Many files and engines use LF anyway, so the tool shows this as a note.
rules.S6: An escape sequence starts and ends with the escape character of MSH-2, for example \F\. HL7 defines a fixed list of codes. \P\ (the truncation character) comes in v2.8. Hex escapes such as \X0D\ need pairs of hex digits. Text formatting commands such as \.br\ are for FT fields. When MSH-2 has no escape character (allowed up to v2.6), the tool skips this check.
rules.S7: The HL7 batch rules allow many messages in one file. The tool explains the text as one message.
rules.V1: MSH-12 holds the HL7 version and is required in every version. From v2.3.1 it has parts, and the version is in the first part.
rules.V2: Versions 2.0, 2.0D, 2.1 and 2.2 are real HL7 versions. The tool explains versions 2.3 to 2.9, so it checks fields only when you pick a version.
rules.V3: Later versions add fields at the end of segments and new delimiter rules. When a message uses them, the sender may follow a later version than MSH-12 says. This is the tool's own hint, not an HL7 rule.
rules.F1: Each HL7 version lists the fields of each segment. A field that was added in a later version does not exist in this version.
rules.F2: Each HL7 version lists the fields of each segment. Up to v2.4 HL7 has no rule for extra fields. From v2.5 local fields at the end of an HL7 segment are allowed, but HL7 advises against them.
rules.F3: W (withdrawn) means HL7 took the field out. Only its number stays, so the later field numbers do not change. The letter W exists from v2.5.
rules.F4: X means the field is not used with this message.
rules.F5: B means the field is kept only for backward compatibility. Senders and receivers may still use it, but HL7 may withdraw it in a later version.
rules.F6: R means required. A field that holds only "" (delete the value) counts as filled. Fields that are required but may be empty (RE, from v2.7) and conditional fields (C) are not checked.
rules.F7: The repeat column of each segment says how many times a field may appear: once, up to a set number, or without a limit.
rules.D1: A DT value is a year, then optionally the month and the day: YYYY[MM[DD]]. That it must be a real date comes from the meaning of a date, not from a written range.
rules.D2: A time stamp is a date, then optionally the hour, minutes, seconds, up to 4 decimals of a second, and a time zone (+ or - and 4 digits). An hour alone is allowed. TS is used up to v2.5.1 and DTM from v2.5. In TS only the first part is checked.
rules.D3: A TM value is HH[MM[SS[.SSSS]]] with an optional time zone, on a 24-hour clock. The hour and minute limits come from the 24-hour clock, not from a written range.
rules.D4: An NM value is an optional + or -, digits, and an optional decimal point. From v2.8 a digit must come before the decimal point.
rules.D5: An SI value is a whole number of 0 or more. From v2.5 it has at most 4 digits, so it goes from 0 to 9999.
rules.G1: Segment names that start with Z are for local use. HL7 never defines them, so the tool cannot know their fields.
rules.G2: The tool explains and checks MSH, EVN, PID, PV1, NK1, ORC, OBR, OBX, AL1 and DG1. Other segments are shown but not checked. This is about the tool, not an HL7 rule.
